relevance_note: One of the ten patients in this HTAD cohort, P10, carries two SLC2A10 variants: 'two heterozygous mutations ... were detected in the SLC2A10 gene associated with ATORS'.
method_note: Built by a short Python script from my own reading; every span checked verbatim by script. Cohort of 10 syndromic HTAD patients; only P10 (SLC2A10, ATORS) is in scope; P01-P08 (FBN1) and P09 (TGFBR2) get no rows. Label 'P10' (text form; Table 2/3 print 'P10 (D.N.B)', and the Discussion once writes 'P010'). Table 2 second SLC2A10 row has an empty Patient ID cell; it continues P10's row. Parents of P10 are mentioned (risk statement; 'testing of the patient's parents will be necessary') but are not tested or described as affected, so no rows; first-degree relatives were 'evaluated clinically' with no individual detail, no rows. Previously reported carriers of c.394C>T (refs 85-88) have no individual-level detail, no rows. Zygosity: the paper states 'compound heterozygous status' and 'most likely in trans', and that four reads suggested trans, but phase was not confirmed by parental testing; Table 2 gives 'Hz' per variant. Recorded compound heterozygous with this caveat. Inheritance not reported: the Abstract calls one SLC2A10 variant 'de novo' ('one de novo and the other a known mutation'), but the Discussion says the parents still need testing, so 'de novo' is not supported by parental testing (rule 8) and appears to mean 'novel' (Table 2: 'new'); this is an internal inconsistency. Age at diagnosis '3 m' from Table 3, whose footnote defines the age column as age at diagnosis; text gives initial evaluation at 3 months and re-evaluation at 1 year (recorded as last evaluation). Table 3 '-' cells counted as excluded using the legend '-: clinical sign absent' (Ao dil/Ao dis, aortic root Z score >= 2, ocular findings); the 'Ocular Findings' '-' excludes only ocular findings as a whole. Family history of AAD '-' not recorded as a feature of the patient. The empty 'Other clinical features' cell is not reported. 'ophthalmological and orthopedic evaluations, which excluded other anomalies associated with ATORS' is too general to exclude any checklist item; not used. Aortic dissection absent does not exclude the broader checklist item 'arterial dissection' (left not reported). Stenosis of the aorta checklist item observed from 'aortic coarctation' in the text (Table 3 lists AAH, not CoA, for P10). No stacked cells in this paper. study_type chosen as case series/cohort.
